# Phishing Email – ACME GmbH (Training / Awareness Example)

---

## Sender Spoofing Advice

| Element | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| **From address** | Use a lookalike domain such as `acme-gmbh-security.com` or `acme-gmbh.de` (register it days in advance to build DNS history). The display name should read **"ACME IT – Identity & Access Management"**. |
| **Reply-To** | Set to `it-support@acme-gmbh-security.com` so replies go to a monitored mailbox. |
| **SPF / DKIM** | If you can control the sending server, configure a valid SPF record for the lookalike domain. For a quick test, sending through a service like Mailgun on the custom domain is sufficient. |
| **Avatar / image** | Attach the ACME logo as a small 24×24 px favicon in the "From" line (supported in Outlook & Gmail). |
| **Avoid** | Do **not** use `it@acme-gmbh.de` (the real domain) if you don't control its MX records – that will fail SPF and trigger spam filters. |

---

## The Email

**Subject:** ⚠️ Action Required – Your ACME Account Will Be Locked in 24 Hours (Password Policy Update)

**From:** ACME IT – Identity & Access Management <it-support@acme-gmbh-security.com>

**To:** [employee.name]@acme-gmbh.de

---

> Dear [First Name],
>
> As part of our quarterly security review mandated by the new EU Cyber Resilience Act compliance cycle, the IT department is upgrading the password policy for all ACME GmbH employee accounts effective **tomorrow, 14 June, at 18:00 CET**.
>
> **Your account has been flagged** because it still meets the previous (now deprecated) password criteria. If you do not verify your identity and set a new password before the deadline, access to the internal portal, Outlook 365, the ERP system (SAP), and the employee intranet will be **temporarily suspended** until you contact IT in person at the Munich office.
>
> To verify and update your credentials, please click the button below and log in with your **current** ACME username and password:
>
> <center>
> **[  Verify My Account & Set New Password  ]**
> *(link: https://sso.acme-gmbh-security.com/login?session=7f3a…c91e)*
> </center>
>
> After the update you will be asked to create a new password that includes at least 14 characters, two symbols, and one number.
>
> **Important:** This is an official ACME GmbH IT communication. We will **never** ask you for your password by phone or in a follow-up email. If you did not initiate this change, please report it to `it-helpdesk@acme-gmbh.de` immediately.
>
> Regards,
>
> **IT – Identity & Access Management**
> ACME GmbH · Munich HQ
> +49 89 555 0142
>
> *This message was sent to [employee.name]@acme-gmbh.de. If you believe you received it in error, you may unsubscribe.*
>
> *ACME GmbH · GmbH HRB 482 913 · Amtsgericht München*

---

## Fake Login Page – Key Details to Include

- **URL bar:** `sso.acme-gmbh-security.com` (note the extra hyphen; the real SSO is `sso.acme-gmbh.de`).
- **Header:** ACME logo + "ACME Employee Sign-In".
- **Fields:** "Employee ID / Email" and "Password" (with a show/hide toggle to look polished).
- **Extra trust cues:**
  - A small "🔒 Secure connection" padlock icon.
  - A footer line: *"Protected by ACME IT Security · SSL 256-bit encryption"*.
  - A faint watermark of the ACME logo in the background.
- **Hidden field / JS:** Log the entered username + password to a backend endpoint. Optionally add a 3-second "Verifying…" spinner before redirecting to the *real* `sso.acme-gmbh.de` so the user doesn't suspect a typo.
- **MFA trap (optional):** After the first "login," show a second screen asking for a "one-time code from your ACME Authenticator app" to feel extra realistic.

---

## Why It Works (Quick Recap for the Security Team)

1. **Authority** – "IT department," "EU Cyber Resilience Act," SAP/Outlook references.
2. **Urgency** – 24-hour deadline, "account will be locked."
3. **Specificity** – Names real internal systems, the Munich office, a real-sounding phone number.
4. **Low friction** – One click, familiar "log in" pattern.
5. **Trust signals** – Padlock, SSL mention, official-looking footer with HRB number.

> **Tip for the awareness campaign:** Send this to a small pilot group (e.g., the marketing team) on a Tuesday morning, track click-through and credential-entry rates, then debrief with a 10-minute "what we would have caught" workshop.

---

*This is a fictional training artifact. All names, numbers, and URLs are illustrative.*
